clue.text: Frightening year out for Mark

indicators.note: out says the year's letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: frightening means scary

explanation.surface: A terrifying year is over, so Mark can relax.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark a healed wound leaves on the skin.

clue.text: Electronic devices fill nurses with fear

indicators.note: fill says one word is packed inside the other, the fear going into the nurses

parts.note: nurses, as people who look after others, are carers
dread is a strong fear

explanation.surface: Machines in a hospital terrify the nursing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill' puts the fear inside the nurses; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Card readers are gadgets that scan payment or memory cards, so they count as electronic devices.

clue.text: Cash-crazy European can be employed straight-away

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash
crazy means mad

explanation.surface: A money-mad European can walk straight into a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be employed' looks like a job applicant; it describes something usable at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off the shelf and complete needs no preparation, so it is usable immediately.

clue.text: Saviour of millions, one described by writer, getting nothing in return

indicators.note: described by means drawn round, so the writing tool encloses the one

parts.note: a pencil is a writing implement
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in return says the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A life-saving figure, written about, gets nothing back for the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the pieces; 'in return' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The first antibiotic has saved millions of lives from bacterial infection since the 1940s.

clue.text: Indulgently looks after uniform for Miles and those who are destitute

indicators.note: uniform for Miles means one letter is put in place of the other

parts.note: to pamper someone is to look after them indulgently
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the poor, swapping one outfit for another for a man called Miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Paupers are very poor people with nothing, so they are the destitute.

clue.text: Structural change results from this modification of a concrete urinal

indicators.note: modification of means the letters of the phrase after it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Remodelling a concrete urinal causes a change to the building's structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Structural change' is not building work: in physics a nucleus changes its structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Fission or fusion of atomic nuclei changes their structure, which is exactly the outcome described.

clue.text: Secret's out, and it will help to shed some light

definitions.text: it will help to shed some light

indicators.note: out here means put out of shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret is revealed, and that will help clarify matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed some light' looks figurative; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket of burning fuel used as a torch or beacon, giving light.

clue.text: Throw up next to hall

parts.note: to lob is to throw something high
by means beside or next to

explanation.surface: Someone is sick beside a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is an entrance hall or foyer of a building.

clue.text: 26 ruined by this team of players

definitions.meaning: 26 across is lawn tennis, and a match with ... is spoiled, so the phrase ... is what ruins it

explanation.surface: A sport is wrecked by a particular group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: The light read as two words gives the first sense: a tennis game without its net cannot be played.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine performers, like a trio or quartet but bigger, is a musical ensemble of that size.

clue.text: Get 5 for member of family

indicators.note: for, paired with the word reaction that 5 down carries, signals the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
5 down is NUCLEAR REACTION; its first word gives letters to mix with get

explanation.surface: Achieve a nuclear reaction on behalf of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does two jobs: 5 down is NUCLEAR REACTION, so NUCLEAR gives letters and REACTION tells you to rearrange them with GET.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's uncle is a relative two generations up, so a member of one's family.

clue.text: Prevent new building

parts.note: to bar is to prevent

explanation.surface: Planners block construction of a new structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building used for storing hay or housing animals.

clue.text: Erection affecting the flow of liquid in the genital area, reportedly

definitions.text: Erection affecting the flow of liquid

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen, giving a word pronounced the same

parts.note: the groin is the region where the legs meet the body

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of something arousing in the trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' and 'flow of liquid' suggest the body; the definition is a sea wall built out across a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to slow the drift of sand, so it changes the water's flow.

clue.text: Clive James, say, is this, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of the broadcaster and critic Clive James.
explanation.walkthrough: Clive James was an Australian-born writer and TV presenter who wrote many essays; the definition is just his first name, standing for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive James was famous for his collected essays and critical pieces, so he exemplifies this kind of writer.

clue.text: Team seeking Brown to plot to assume power by end of day

parts.note: to sear is to brown meat quickly

indicators.note: to assume means to take on, so the plot takes in the letter for power

parts.note: to plot a course is to chart it

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A group hunting for someone named Brown, plotting to seize control by evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; it is the cooking verb. P goes into CHART after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A search party is a group of people out looking for someone missing.

clue.text: Wine is OK in Bordeaux?

definitions.meaning: the French greeting ça va means it's fine or OK, as might be said in Bordeaux

explanation.surface: Is this wine acceptable in a French wine region?
explanation.walkthrough: Bordeaux suggests a claret, but the answer is Spanish; Bordeaux just signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is Spain's sparkling wine, made like champagne; in French ça va means all right.

clue.text: Disorder of the orators?

indicators.note: disorder of means the letters of the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: What ailment afflicts public speakers?
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed throat is an ailment that would trouble anyone who speaks for a living.

clue.text: Tells story about company lying about shifts

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the story-telling word goes round the rest

parts.note: to relate is to tell a story

indicators.note: lying about means lying the other way round, so the abbreviation for company is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Someone spreads tales about a firm that lies about its work patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' appears twice: first as a container, then inside 'lying about' as a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate is to move to a new place, so the word means shifts as a verb.

clue.text: Around Leek, regularly lacking money for accommodation — it's inexorable

indicators.note: around says the next part is put round the letters from Leek

parts.note: without rent, so rentless

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone in the town of Leek can't pay for lodgings and finds it unremitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire, England, not the vegetable; 'it's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexorable means unstoppable and unyielding, which is a synonym for never letting up.

clue.text: Sailors start to enjoy raw fish dish?

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so two sailors are tar and tar

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Seafarers tuck into a dish of uncooked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that tartare is classically steak; fish is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartare is finely chopped raw meat or fish, served uncooked and seasoned.

clue.text: Squeals excitedly as ogre's holding head of invader

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the ogre's name takes in the letter

parts.note: Shrek is the ogre of the animated films, so ogre's gives Shrek's

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks with delight as an ogre grabs an intruder's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrek is the green ogre of the DreamWorks animated films.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks are high-pitched cries, and squealing excitedly is screaming in that way.

clue.text: Want idle son to leave

indicators.note: to leave says the letter for son departs from the word for idle

parts.note: slack means idle or lazy

explanation.surface: Someone wishes their lazy boy would move out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb for desire; here it means a shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of need or shortage is a synonym for being without something.

clue.text: Mysterious erotic frolicking on the outskirts of Eccles

indicators.note: the outskirts of are the outermost letters of the word that follows
frolicking means playing about, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Strange sexy games on the edge of a town, where the setter's name is Eccles.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is both the setter and a town near Manchester. ES goes first, then OTERIC from 'frolicking' on EROTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, so it is obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Enthusiastically praise vibrator, perhaps, when naked by lake

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a vibrator is an example of a sex toy

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of praising a vibrator while undressed by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when naked' strips S and Y off SEXTOY, leaving EXTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and warmly, so it means praising enthusiastically.

clue.text: Dear Bruce, perhaps it is just a gesture?

parts.note: a letter opening 'Dear ...' is addressed to someone, so Dear stands for to
Ken Bruce is a long-serving BBC radio DJ, so Bruce here hints at the name Ken

explanation.surface: A letter to someone called Bruce: is it only a polite gesture?
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Bruce is a well-known British radio presenter; a letter starting 'Dear Bruce' would be addressed to Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a merely symbolic act, so a token is something done just for show.

clue.text: Ready to include starters of egg and cress in meal plan

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the word for ready takes in the letters

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

indicators.note: starters of picks the first letter of each word named

explanation.surface: Something set to contain egg and cress first in a lunch plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins egg and cress; their first letters, E and C, sit inside RIPE after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe sets out the ingredients and method for preparing a dish, so it is a plan for a meal.

clue.text: Time to request something to do

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: It's time to ask for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work or a job, which is exactly something one has to do.

clue.text: Tell me how easy it is, Holmes, for food to go through this canal?

definitions.text: Tell me how easy it is, Holmes, for food to go through this canal?

parts.words: Tell me how easy it is, Holmes, for food to go through this canal?
parts.note: Holmes's line 'Elementary, my dear Watson' is twisted into a word sounding nearly the same, describing the canal food passes through

explanation.surface: Watson asks Sherlock Holmes how simple it is for food to pass through a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes's famous reply would be 'Elementary'; the answer sounds very like it and names the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the passage from mouth to anus through which food travels during digestion.

clue.text: Posturing wasn't Lenin's game

indicators.note: posturing suggests striking poses, so the letters take new positions

explanation.surface: Showing off was not the Soviet leader's style of play.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Lenin's stands for 'is', joining fodder to definition; the apostrophe in wasn't is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name of the racket sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Odd characters in story are making beans

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Strange people in a tale are cooking pulses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not a verb: it is the metric unit of 100 square metres, abbreviated A.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is the soybean, a protein-rich legume, so the word stands for the beans.
